title: PPC exp loses sparse low components at tiny positive arguments
description: Both LLVM majors violate the 0.2.12 section 13.4 one-local-ulp bound for PPC exp at exact x=2^-700. Native constrained modes 0,1,3,4 return (1,+0); upward returns (1,2^-105), flags16. Exact series bounds for 0<x<1/2 give 1+x<exp(x)<1+x+x*x. The adjacent canonical pairs bracketing exp(x) are L=(1,2^-700), U=(1,2^-700+2^-752): both canonical and binary64 low components adjacent; other high bins are far away. Because x*x < (U-L)/2, nearest/down/towardzero must select L, upward U. Returning 1 has error greater than x, i.e. greater than 2^52 local ulps; returning 1+2^-105 is still farther. This is a full-domain numerical implementation bug, not a contract ambiguity. Add an independent exact-bound diagnostic witness and retain wvh pending full-domain repair/evidence; do not narrow source precision, reject inputs, weaken tests, or claim measured MPFR sweeps establish the envelope.
design: For valid canonical x=h+l, 0<|x|<=2^-112 implies exp(x)=1+z with RN64(1+any selected low)=1. Taylor gives0<z-x<x². Let2^E<=|h|<2^(E+1). Canonical nonoverlap gives|x|<2|h|; hence z-x<2^-111|h|<2^(E-110). A nonzero gap from h+l to a neighbouring binary64 midpoint is >=2^(E-107) (including the asymmetric power-of-two bin); subnormal half-grid gaps are larger. Thus nearest low rounding changes only at exact input midpoints, always upward. For directed modes, exp(x)-1>h iff x>log(1+h). Put h=M*2^e with at most53 significand bits, q=2^(2e-1). The logarithm residual is-h²/2+R, with sign(R)=sign(h), |R|<|h|³, and |h|³/q=2|h|M²<1/32. If negative l has exponent>=2e-1, any nonzero difference l+h²/2 is an integer multiple of q, so R cannot reverse it. If l has smaller exponent, h is normal and |l|<2^52*q while h²/2>=2^104*q, so the gap is much larger still. At exact quadratic equality, sign R settles the side: positive h selects below h, negative h above. Nonnegative l always selects above h. Compare h²/2 against |l| exactly at quantum2^-2149 in4352 bits. Directed output is the appropriate adjacent f64 field around h; nearest output is selected by exact midpoint distances. Zero gives exact1; nonzero rational x has transcendental exp(x), so final flags are inexact only. Total near1 excludes underflow/overflow/domain flags. Independent test oracle instead encloses z between x+x²/2+x³/6 and that plus x⁴ and requires both endpoints to round identically. Full numerical contract and all operation domains remain required; this increment is a proved path within the still-open global wvh task.
notes:
Reproduction is tests/ppc_exp_sparse_witness.py, using independent rational Taylor bounds and canonical high-bin adjacency. timeout 30s python3 -u -I tests/ppc_exp_sparse_witness.py verified both published majors: each plain result provably outside the one-ulp envelope, and all five constrained modes disagree with exact neighbour selection (12 disagreements total). All actual flags are16; this witness is specifically a numerical result failure, not evidence of a flag failure for this input.
Red-green work: tests/test_ppc_exp.py first fails on the published LLVM18 exp(2^-700) result (high1, low0). Staged exact-sum path now passes12276 value/mode/flag checks on LLVM18. Proof covers every finite |x|<=2^-538 of either sign: Taylor bounds give0<exp(x)-1-x<2^-1076, inputs lie on the2^-1074 grid, endpoints/midpoints on its half-grid. A strict upward perturbation determines binary64 low rounding exactly; total near1 means only final inexact, never intermediate underflow. Tests sweep every power exponent down to-1074, sparse positive/negative low components and exact low midpoints. LLVM23 and full publication gate still pending; wvh full-domain work remains open.
LLVM23 focused stage also passed12276 exact checks. Both exp-fix publications are now built (before the next independent gko specialization); pending a combined full producer gate. Intermediate hashes: LLVM18 bc76775cf893d856aae857d23195df268d9abb45b50cf7760c70d0220140a79929 manifest90e0bb01efea63746815a897cdc7d45db82a180862a0951433124f2ddb5e24c7; LLVM23 bc69bd5b8be13ec7d825bf9d2840f738a7b2b67d1cb1f80dac2d92e842d0fe8e01 manifesta5c0e39e12fc4b3dcd325537045e45b4681b019c1c055b55b22d64451b864e7a.
Extended the proven path to ALL canonical finite |x|<=2^-112, with no narrowing of the full contract. The broader regression first failed at-2^-537, then new staged LLVM18 passed24930 checks. Nearest rounding uses exact input low-midpoint gaps; directed rounding compares l to-h*h/2 exactly in4352-bit integers, with the cubic sign settling exact cancellation (via monotonic exp/log(1+h)). Independent rational oracle bounds exp(x)-1 by x+x²/2+x³/6 and that plus x⁴, requiring both bounds to round identically. Added quadratic-cancellation neighbours, both signs, worst-range edges and full53-bit significands. This supersedes the initial quarter-grid-only implementation; full wvh still retains obligations outside this path.

title: Clarify canonical PPC nearest-even parity at zero-low component transitions
description: Independent exact witness verifies an inconsistency/ambiguity in dialect 0.2.12 section 13.1 nearest-even canonical-pair selection when one candidate low component is zero. Command: timeout 30s python3 -u -I tests/ppc_zero_low_witness.py (exit 0 verifies the witness, not arithmetic conformance). Let u=2^-1074, h=1+2^-52 (f64 0x3ff0000000000001), a=(h,u), b=(1/2,+0), c=(h/2,+0). All are canonical finite pairs. Exact FMA is h+u/2; its two adjacent canonical neighbours are L=(h,+0), U=(h,u), both at distance u/2. Every binary64 and pair sum is an integer multiple of u, proving adjacency. The published rule uses high significand when low is zero: L therefore has odd high parity, while U has odd low subnormal significand 1. Neither candidate is even, so the literal requirement cannot select an even neighbour for this valid input. Required exact contract change: define parity at zero-low transitions, e.g. use zero low significand's even parity whenever either candidate has a nonzero low, with high-significand fallback only when BOTH candidate low components are zero; otherwise specify an explicit deterministic rule for equal/no-even parity. Preserve all formats, operations and input-domain capability. Native evidence also shows both existing majors return L with flags=0, although either nearest result must raise inexact=16 and no underflow (total is near one). That implementation flag bug remains part of 4yg. No narrowed subset, trap or unsupported result is proposed. Cross-repo spec bead request is recorded for the orchestrator under COMMON14.
notes:
The same ambiguity also blocks incoming IEEE conversion, with a verified binary128 input. Let H be binary64 bits 0x0030000000000001, u=2^-1074, V=H+u/2. V is exactly binary128 bits 0x3c030000000000001200000000000000. Adjacent canonical pairs (H,0) and (H,u) have odd/odd parity and equal distance u/2. tests/ppc_zero_low_witness.py now verifies binary128 exact representability and canonical adjacency as well as FMA. Both native conversions select the lower pair and report flags24 (legacy underflow), whereas any nearest result must report only inexact16 since the total is normal. A published parity decision is needed for both FMA and incoming IEEE conversion.

title: Specify signaling constrained comparison ABI without losing fcmps flags
description: Contract clarification blocker, no capability removed. Determining dialect 0.2.10 §13.5 sentence: llvm.experimental.constrained.<op> becomes the soft-float call of §13.1 with suffix _rm and an extra i32 R operand; non-ignore exception behavior ORs IEEE flags into __bennett_rt_fenv.flags. Both LLVM 18 and 23 define constrained.fcmp (quiet) and constrained.fcmps (signaling). §13.1 only supplies cmp_B(C,C,i32 P), where P is restricted to LLVM predicates 0..15. The same carrier operands, P and R cannot tell these two exception behaviors apart for quiet-NaN inputs. Required exact contract change: specify a distinct cmps_B_rm(C,C,i32 P,i32 R) spelling (or an explicit signaling operand/encoded predicate extension), including quiet-NaN invalid semantics and the normalisation mapping. Current cmp_B_rm implements quiet comparison, raising invalid on signaling NaN; signaling comparison remains required and tracked, never silently treated as quiet.
notes: Exact signaling/quiet ABI ambiguity filed as b-dialect-spec-21a (consumer,dialect,arith), with §13.1/13.5 quote and both readings. Quiet cmp_B_rm is present for all seven formats; signaling remains required and cannot be substituted silently. Plugin unchanged.
close_reason: The 0.2.12 distinct signaling ABI is implemented and numerically verified by child chn.1 on both majors, including exhaustive small-format NaN payloads and exact flags. Full dual-major scripts/gate passed after adding all required export/exercise cases; no unresolved signaling ABI remains.

title: Own-format deterministic transcendental libm and arbitrary-width powi

Determining dialect 0.2.10 §13.4 sentences: All seven source formats remain covered on every supported platform; a format different from D is neither rejected nor trapped. These linked bennett-arith/runtimes functions implement the named operation numerically in B, using the same deterministic, versioned implementation in both builds. Implement sin cos tan asin acos atan atan2 sinh cosh tanh exp exp2 exp10 log log2 log10 pow sincos sincospi, plus powi_iK for K other than implemented i32. Include own-format precision, zeros, NaNs, reduction extremes, subnormal-output sweeps and all aggregate field orders. Correct rounding not required for §13.4, determinism is.
notes:
All seven own-format libm families implemented and MPFR-tested; 130464 main +137860 exhaustive/PPC/rounding +14655 subnormal/overflow checks per major. Ordinary maximum reported error 0.5 ulp, not a correct-rounding/global-bound proof. All exact-width powi supported by generator; ten default widths through i1025, custom i7 publication executed. Focused final boundary: LLVM18/23 MAX_INT_BITS is inclusive 8388608. Exact i8388608 powi wrapper assembles/verifies on both majors. Default bitcodes remain byte-identical to bb79deb; manifest provenance updated.

title: bennett-isa-ref lags ISA 0.9 K4: inverse_pair claims, entry budget and qinplace ins list
description: At bennett-isa-spec HEAD the metadata schema's expected union has no inverse_pair and inverse_pairs entries reject budget (metadata_schema.rs:136, 195), and the object parser rejects qinplace with an (ins) list ('result/operand count differs', §4.8). Remove both workarounds when the interpreter catches up (follow-ups b-isa-spec-fuk.3-.7 cover parametrised qinplace; the schema item has no bead there that this stream could find).
notes: Also: Object::verify_certificate (library only, the CLI never calls it) cannot verify any 0.9 table claim: the claims parser requires K13 {before,after} rows while verify_claim reads arrays, so it rejects the spec's own conformance/fixtures/controlled-action-09/controlled.bisa with '§9.1: expected JSON array', and array rows fail the schema instead. Evidence: one-off harness over 59 published objects and that fixture. tests/circuits/test_objects.py replays table rows itself, bit-sliced and through run-action.

title: Dialect 8.7/TDL-5(b): publish symbol names and signatures for library bijections
description: Dialect 8.7 says a library bijection lowers to the library's permutation action and TDL-5(b) lists the operations, but no symbol or signature is named, so plugin and arith cannot agree except by convention. docs/circuits-port.md proposes arith.bij.{add,sub,addk,subk,xor,xork,rotl,rotr,neg,bswap,addmodk,addmod,mulmodk}.* with x mut and k in. Exact change: the dialect adopts or replaces this table, including the qinplace token argument of the modular forms.

title: ISA 6.2: admit certified workspace cleanup in library permutation actions, for gate-level modular arithmetic
description: addmod_const_gates, addmod_in_gates and mulmod_const_gates (adders/constructions.py) are clean on every basis input by exhaustive test but bennett-isa-ref rejects them with §6.2 because their flags depend on x and x changes. The only legal form today is qinplace through lifted oracles, so the published modular bijections cost the §11 row expansion, not 9(2W-1) or 20W^2+3W-4 Toffoli. Exact change needed in ISA: a verification field analogous to 5.6 borrow_frames (or 4.5's certified t and f) by which an exhaustive or library claim discharges clean workspace at qfree.

title: ISA 6.2/6.4: admit a T-optimal temp-AND so Gidney's adder reaches 4(W-1) T
description: tests/circuits/test_adders.py pins that bennett-isa-ref rejects a 4-T AND (h t cx tdg cx t cx tdg h sdg) whose value has a lasting reader, with §6.2 'released value has not been uncomputed', because h makes it an other value and 6.4 reserves measurement-based cleanup. So arith.add.gidney costs 14(W-1) T with exact ccx. Exact change needed in ISA: a provenance rule treating an exact permutation-valued sequence on clean workspace as perm (or a target scheme for ccx with a clean target), plus the normative 6.4 fixup and its certificate kind (17 item 6). North star: the compiler chooses measurement-based versus unitary uncomputation.
